evidence: Searches found EHD/ionic-wind fans (cooling, ventilation) and fanless wind-driven DAC contactors (Georgia Tech WEDAC) separately, but nothing pairing an ionic-wind fan with a DAC sorbent contactor.

US patent 8603024 describes a glaucoma drainage device whose valve is governed by an electro-osmotic membrane between electrodes; other patents cover electrolysis/electrocapillary pumps with IOP sensors, but no working demonstration found.
US patent 8353928 ('Electrochemical wound therapy') claims electro-osmotically moving wound fluid from a cavity over the wound into a chamber/sponge; no clinical or prototype demonstration found.

Messerli lab (SDSU) demonstrated electrokinetic (electro-osmotic) perfusion through 3D matrices that reduced cell mortality more consistently than pressure-driven perfusion, framed as keeping artificial tissue alive before vascularization (not yet multi-cm constructs).
US patent 7709129 describes capillary condensation of vapour in a flow passage with the condensed water moved out by electro-osmosis; no working humidity harvester of this kind found.

Cullet sorters use IR/optical opacity, XRF, induction heating or Steinert's HR-glass upgrade; index-matched immersion appears only as a bench test for identifying borosilicate, not as a sorting process.

An NUS 2026 Nature Communications mechano-electroluminescent e-skin maps plantar pressure visually for gait and diabetic-ulcer risk, but it is electrically driven rather than self-glowing mechanoluminescent crystals; no ML footprint mat found.
Limb-swelling wearables use capacitive sleeves, strain bands or 3D bodysuits, and moire strain indicators exist for structures, but no moire band for limb circumference was found.

Patents describe fluid-filled bladders/capsules under casts linked to a pressure sensor or indicator with an alarm for excessive pressure (e.g. US 4858620), and a 2022 study tested an under-cast Bluetooth pressure sensor; no product found.
Battery swelling is detected with per-cell pressure/force or resistance sensors between cells; no design using linked fluid pockets feeding one gauge was found.

US patent 4184805 describes airfoils driven into flutter by a fluid stream with the oscillation used for work including pumping, and flutter hydropower papers mention irrigation channels; no working flutter irrigation pump found.
The Arch Mission Foundation has announced plans for Arch Libraries at Sun-Earth L4/L5 (target 2027); its existing archive is in heliocentric orbit, and no L4/L5 archive has flown.

Emulsion-based time-temperature indicators exist in patents and an EU project (emulsion destabilization causing visible change, three-phase emulsions), but none found using Ostwald ripening plus light scattering as the clock.
Searches found microLED optrodes, fibre-reflectometry and frequency-multiplexed recording on one wire, but no photoconductive, light-addressed electrode array for neural recording.
Searches found Leidenfrost droplet physics and NaCl droplet crystallization studies, and scaling-control ZLD crystallizers, but no Leidenfrost-based brine dryer.
A 2002 Desalination paper argues water hammer from a hydro-ram can supply reverse-osmosis pressure, and a HeroX concept proposes a ram-pump-fed RO system; no tested prototype found.

Acoustic standing-wave trapping of microplastics is built (HKRITA Acousweep, EchoGrid) and UV photodegradation is studied separately, but nothing combines acoustic trapping with targeted UV breakdown.
Perimeter-style long-term retardant patents claim magnesium/calcium chloride solutions pull moisture into fuels to retard fire; no independent field trials of a hygroscopic-salt firebreak found.
Penn State proposes spintronic PUFs exploiting stochastic domain-wall pinning/depinning, and a patent uses magnetic noise spectra as a PUF signature; no demonstrated Barkhausen-noise PUF chip found.
US patent 9988517 'Physical colorants for plastics based on the Christiansen effect' proposes glass-particle/polymer index-matched colorants; no Christiansen-coloured textile fibre found.
Dendrometers for irrigation scheduling are commercial and moire displacement amplification exists elsewhere, but no moire-based trunk/stem dendrometer was found.

Active CSF shunts use electroactive polymers, electromechanical or electrokinetic actuators, and capillary-electrowetting valves exist separately, but no electrowetting hydrocephalus shunt valve was found.

CSF lab practice already uses side-scattered light (Tyndall effect: a tube lit at 90 degrees looks 'sparkling' at low cell counts) to flag raised cells; the phone-camera laser quantification is the only new part (evidence from lab teaching material).
Mosquito pupa sex sorters use sieves, plates and machine vision (ORINNO, WOLBAKI, Science Robotics sorter); acoustic sorting found only for nematodes in microchannels.
Reconfigurable water storm shelters (NASA RadWorks water wall, TransHab fill/drain tank) and repositionable shield patents exist, but none moves water by electro-osmosis through porous walls.
